prerequisites: It is recommended to have passed Graphic Expression I

learning_outcomes.text: Capacity for spatial vision and knowledge of graphic representation techniques, both by traditional methods of metric and descriptive geometry, and by computer-aided design applications

Capacity for the drafting and development of projects in the field of mechanical engineering, for the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing processes
Capacity for handling specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards
Capacity for the interpretation of technical projects and reports
Demonstrate the ability to analyze and synthesize
Acquire the ability to effectively solve problems
Acquire skills related to the use of computer programs for calculation, data analysis and processing, within their field of application
Develop the ability to transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences
Information search and management skill
Possess the ability to make decisions
Develop critical reasoning
Develop interpersonal skills
Develop the ability to work in a team
Ability to apply knowledge to practice
Acquire the ability for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and continuous training
Develop the ability to adapt to new situations
Ability to generate new ideas (creativity)
Ability to work autonomously
Show initiative and entrepreneurial spirit
Motivation for quality and continuous improvement
Achievement motivation
Become aware of issues related to the environment
Complete the knowledge of standardization and technical drawing from Graphic Expression I.
Be able to interpret drawings of mechanical assemblies, their montages, their exploded views, and parts lists of different mechanisms.
Be able to represent and designate standardized elements of industrial drawing, according to standards.
Acquire knowledge of standardization for geometric and dimensional tolerances, surface qualities, and functional dimensioning.
Know the symbology and types of diagrams for electrical, pneumatic, and piping installations to interpret their various diagrams. Be able to interpret diagrams of industrial projects.
Acquire basic knowledge of construction drawing, so that students can represent and interpret industrial installations in construction drawings.
Be able to create assembly drawings of mechanisms, their montages, exploded views, and parts lists, both sketched and by computer.
Functionally dimension the drawings for finished product definition.
Be able to create different types of diagrams for electrical, pneumatic, and piping installations, as well as the construction drawings necessary to indicate the various industrial installations.

syllabus_topics: Graphic Expression in Engineering
Mechanical Assemblies
Introduction to industrial drawing.
Assembly drawing, exploded view, and standardized material designation.
Representation and dimensioning of threads.
Dismountable joints. Types of joints. Designation of standardized elements.
Springs. Types and representation of springs.
Bearings and rolling bearings. Representation, designation, selection, and fastening and protection elements for rolling bearings.
Representation of welded joints.
Functional Dimensioning
Surface qualities. Roughness. Types of surfaces. Symbols. Indications in the drawing of surface quality and type.
Dimensional tolerance. Definitions. How to indicate tolerances in dimensions. Calculation of the magnitude of the tolerance zone. Systems and selection of fits. General dimensional tolerances.

Geometric tolerances. Introduction. Application of geometric tolerances. Tolerances of form, orientation, position, and runout. Indication of geometric tolerances in drawings. Application of the maximum material principle. General geometric tolerances.

Functional dimensioning. General problem statement. Dimension chain. Calculation of the condition dimension. Distribution of tolerance in the dimension chain. Influence of geometric tolerances in the dimension chain. Dimension transfer.
Drawing and Design of Installations

Drawing and design of pneumatic installation. Bases for the design and interpretation of pneumatic diagrams. Actuators. Distributor valves. Shut-off valves. Types of diagrams. Symbology. Design of simple diagrams.
Electrical drawing in building. Symbols of electrification in building. Electrical diagrams in building. Connection installation between the public grid and the interior installation.
Electrical drawing in industrial installations. Electrical control circuits for motors. Symbols of electrical circuits. Types of electrical circuit diagrams. The main circuit and the control circuit.
Computer-Aided Drawing and Design
Drawing of 2D and 3D installation plans and diagrams.
Modeling for additive manufacturing and 3D printing.
teaching_methods: Practical classes (small groups on drawing board and CAD)
Preparation of assignments, reports, memoirs, and evaluation tests
Theoretical part delivering fundamentals of Geometry, Representation Systems, and Industrial Drawing Standardization.
Drawing board practical part with manual application exercises.
Introduction to obtaining 3D objects using appropriate software.
Development of a tutored group final project/work using CAD tools.
assessment_rules: In the 2nd call, the procedure for recovering the continuous assessment part (Drawing Board Practices, Computer Practices, Project work) will be agreed with the teaching staff, with its percentage in the final grade remaining the same as in the ordinary assessment. The rest of the assessment system remains exactly as indicated in the ordinary assessment. A minimum score of 3 points is required for Theoretical Evaluation and Automatisms, 3.5 points for Manual Drawing of Mechanisms Evaluation, and 3 points for CAD Mechanism Design Evaluation. In all cases and calls, if the student does not meet any of the minimum scores mentioned, the overall grade for the course will be calculated according to the UBU Evaluation Regulations.
